newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on Ramos health.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on Ramos health.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed firmer at 26.297 to the dollar from yesterday's close of 26.30 on news that President Fidel Ramos has fully recovered from surgery performed on him a day before, traders said.

"The peso strengthened because of the good news over Ramos's health," one trader at a foreign bank said, citing news that Ramos was back on his feet and already met cabinet ministers in his hospital room.
The peso hit an intra-day low of 26.307 early in the session, but rebounded to as high as 26.292 by late morning.

The dealer added that banks sold some of the dollars they amassed yesterday in reaction to the news that Ramos underwent a surgery to remove a cholesterol block in his right carotid artery. The peso fell to a low of 26.325 before recovering in the afternoon.
The Central Bank bought about $19 million at 26.295 to keep the peso from rising too fast, dealers added.
Another trader said inflows from overseas workers and portfolio investments contributed to the strength of the local currency.
Turnover was moderate at $146.5 million in an abbreviated session. The market was closed by noon as most banks declared a half-day holiday ahead of Christmas.
The peso-dollar market will be closed on Tuesday for Christmas Day.
